Actually scheme A vs B: OIML-CS has Scheme A (certificates issued by issuing authorities) and Scheme B (utilizing existing certificates). R60 certificates issued by NMi as OIML Issuing Authority NL1 → Scheme A. The issuer is "NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1" — so scheme A.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["CB069"]
- module_designation: "Analog load cell"? The cert says "A single point load cell, with strain gauges." Module designation — R60 load cells are analog typically; the cert doesn't state "analog load cell" explicitly. Hmm. Rule says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since not stated, I could put "Analog load cell" — but don't fabricate. Actually the characteristics like rated output 2 mV/V suggest analog, but the cert doesn't say. Safer: null. Hmm, but many R60 certs list "Analog load cell" module. Here it's not stated, so null. Actually let me reconsider — module_designation null is fine.
- description: "A single point load cell, with strain gauges."

Model family: The Emax is "5 kg up to and including 25 kg" — a range, not multiple discrete variants. So no model_family needed (single model CB069 with Emax range 5–25 kg). Rules say include model_family ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Here it's one type CB069 with an Emax range. So omit model_family, put Emax as type_level range: {min: 5, max: 25}, unit kg.

Characteristics type_level:
- maximum_capacity (Emax): 5 to 25 kg → value {min:5, max:25}, unit_symbol "kg"
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg → value 0, unit "kg"
- accuracy_class: "C" → string value, unit null
- rated_output: 2 mV/V → value 2, unit_symbol "mV/V"
- max_number_of_load_cell_intervals (n): 3000, dimensionless → value 3000, unit null. Label canonical: "maximum_number_of_intervals" — per examples "Max. number of load cell intervals n_LC" → max_load_cell_intervals_nlc. Here it's (n) not n_LC. I'll use "maximum_number_of_load_cell_intervals_n" or simply "max_number_of_intervals_n". Example: `Max. number of load cell intervals n<sub>LC</sub>` → `max_load_cell_intervals_nlc`. Analogously "Maximum number of load cell intervals (n)" → `max_load_cell_intervals_n`. I'll use that.
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 10000 (Y = Emax/vmin). Label per example: `ratio_y_emax_over_vmin`. Value 10000.
- ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: 3000 (Z = Emax/(2*DR)). Label: "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr" or "ratio_z". I'll use "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr".
- input_impedance: 425 Ω ± 25 Ω → this is nominal with tolerance. Could represent as value 425 with tolerance? Schema only has value/unit. Options: value {min:400, max:450} unit Ω. ±25 on 425 → 400–450. That's a reasonable structured representation. Alternatively value "425 ± 25" — but strict rule wants numbers. I'll do {min: 400, max: 450}, unit "Ω". Hmm, but that changes semantics slightly (a tolerance rather than range). I think range is acceptable. Or keep value 425 and add nothing for tolerance — loses info. I'll go with the min/max.
- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- fraction_plc (apportionment factor pLC): 0,7 → 0.7, unit null. Label per example: `apportionment_factor_plc`. I'll use that.
- humidity_class: "NH" → string value.
- safe_overload: 150% of Emax → value 150, unit "%" plus separate reference characteristic "safe_overload_reference": "Emax" per rule 3 example.
- output_impedance: 350 Ω ± 5 Ω → {min: 345, max: 355}, unit "Ω"
- recommended_excitation: 12 V AC/DC → per rule, split: recommended_excitation_voltage value 12, unit "V"; power supply type? "AC / DC" — could add recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC". The rule example splits voltage/frequency/type. Here AC/DC isn't frequency. I'll add recommended_excitation_voltage (12 V) and maybe recommended_excitation_type "AC/DC". Hmm, keep it: recommended_excitation_voltage: 12 V; excitation_maximum similar: excitation_maximum_voltage: 20 V. Alternatively keep original label "recommended_excitation" with value 12 unit V and a note. The rule 3 explicitly instructs splitting combined values. I'll do:
  - recommended_excitation_voltage: 12, "V"
  - excitation_type? Better: recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC" string.
  - maximum_excitation_voltage: 20, "V"
  - maybe maximum_excitation_type: "AC/DC". Could combine as excitation_type: "AC / DC" applying to both. I'll include a single "excitation_type": "AC/DC".
- transducer_material: "Aluminum alloy" → string.
- atmospheric_protection: "Silicone and butyl rubber coating" → string.

Note "The characteristics for n_max and Y can be reduced separately." — this is a note; could go in description or footnotes? Not a footnote with marker. I could omit or include as a note. Schema has no "notes" field. Could add to footnotes with marker? No marker. I'll omit, or include in certificate? Rules say don't fabricate; there's no place. I'll skip it. Actually could include as matrix description... no. Skip.
